title: LISTEN: ‘Roland Martin Unfiltered’ Rides Midterm Elections Momentum After Historic Vote
description: On today’s episode of Variety‘s “Strictly Business” podcast, digital news entrepreneur Roland Martin discusses the growth of his “Roland Martin Unf
body:
On today’s episode of Variety‘s “Strictly Business” podcast, digital news entrepreneur Roland Martin discusses the growth of his “Roland Martin Unfiltered” program and how it gained momentum during the buildup to this last week’s historic midterm elections.

	Martin’s daily political news and commentary roundtable program went on a barnstorming tour over the three weeks leading up to Election Day on Nov. 3. The show targeted key areas in the South and Southeast where the protection of voting rights, affordability, the relentless GOP attack on DEI and other issues had already fired up voters.
	

	“Twelve cities in fifteen days. It was Little Rock, Arkansas. Fairfax, Virginia. Lansing, Michigan. We came home for a day. Then it was like Indianapolis, Atlanta and then we were in Jackson, Mississippi, Baton Rouge, Louisiana, Miami Gardens, West Palm Beach, Tallahassee, Florida. Back to Atlanta and Lithonia, Georgia again. Baton Rouge. then. Arlington, Texas. Dallas, Texas. Houston, Texas. Fort Bend County. And then came home two days before the election,” Martin says. 

	“It was absolutely crazy. the first week I had our 35-foot bus on the road. And then that second week I had that and the Sprinter [van] on the road. And we were flying into a city, doing the show, go to the hotel, put all of our suitcases in the Sprinter and then would just pack overnight clothes. They would drive to the next city overnight. We would then fly to the next city. Uber to the hotel, check in. Go set up. Do the show. Repeat, rinse, repeat. I was a show host, a producer, a travel agent, a logistical coordinator.  It was crazy.”
	

	Martin, an alumnus of CNN, TV One and Tom Joyner’s radio program, says the tour reflected the freedom and flexibility offered by working in digital media. And it all has the potential to reach viewers in a different way than a traditional news program.

	“What’s so different from linear is that you’re really touching viewers. You’re really communicating with them. I’m not spending three, four, five, six minutes on a segment. Sometimes I’m doing twenty, thirty minutes doing deep dives,” Martin says. “I’m not trying to do a mainstream show. I am not trying to replicate MS NOW, CNN, ABC, NBC, CBS, Fox News, or any of those people. We break all the rules. We’re not trying to be slick. I’ll grab my DJI action camera and I’m shooting stuff and it’s totally unconventional. But we’re serving the audience and communicating them in a different way.”

schema.headline: LISTEN: ‘Roland Martin Unfiltered’ Rides Midterm Elections Momentum After Historic Vote

title: French Judo Legend Teddy Riner Announces 2027 Presidential Bid, Drawing Praise From Emmanuel Macron
description: French judo superstar Teddy Riner, a five-time Olympic gold medalist and multiple world champion, has announced that he is running for president of
body:
French judo superstar Teddy Riner, a five-time Olympic gold medalist and multiple world champion, has announced that he is running for president of France in 2027 in a fiery speech posted on social media.

	The athlete, who has never held political office but is one of France’s most recognizable and popular sporting figures, portrayed himself as a political outsider determined to stand for ordinary French citizens which he feels have been let down.
	

	Riner’s announcement comes at a particularly turbulent moment in France, just five months before a presidential election that has exposed deep divisions across the political spectrum.

	The far-right party Rassemblement National is dominating the polls by a wide margin, with Marine Le Pen drawing between 33% and 37% of first-round voting intentions in recent surveys, roughly twice the support of her closest rivals. Jean-Luc Mélenchon, who leads the radical-left party La France Insoumise, has been gaining ground and is polling at around 17% to 19%, while the political center remains fragmented, with no candidate emerging to succeed Emmanuel Macron. The country has also been rocked by weeks of mass protests over the soaring cost of living and conditions in schools which escalated into violent riots.

	“My name is Teddy Riner, and today I’m telling you straight to your face: I am a candidate in the 2027 presidential election,” he said while facing the camera and sitting at a desk in a presidential-style setting while bookshelves and a tricolor French flag in the background.


	“I know what people are going to say about me: ‘He’s crazy,’ ‘He’s not part of the establishment,’ ‘He doesn’t know the rules,’ ‘He’s never been involved in politics.’ But ask yourselves this question: What is really crazy today?”
	

	Riner went on to paint a bleak picture of France, citing growing public debt, economic hardship and a breakdown of law and order.

	“Is it crazy to refuse to watch France collapse under the weight of its debt, a little more every day? To see a country so rich pretend that it is poor?” he asked.

	Riner criticized what he described as an unfair system that places an excessive burden on working people.

	“Is it crazy to reject the hypocrisy of a system where those who get up early, work hard and follow the rules have no choice but to pay for everyone else?”

	Macron reacted warmly to Riner’s announcement in an interview with the French broadcaster France 5 welcoming his decision to enter politics and praising his sense of duty. “Teddy Riner is a tremendous athlete who makes our country proud,” Macron said. “I supported him in competitions and as an athlete, and he is a committed man.”

	Macron, who cannot seek a third consecutive presidential term in 2027, applauded the prospect of citizens from outside the political establishment taking part in the national debate. 

	“Political life, the life of the nation, does not belong to professionals,” Macron said, alluding to his own path, as he came into politics a decade ago after working in investment banking at Rothschild. “The life of the nation belongs to women and men who want to give their time, who are ready to commit themselves and fight difficult battles to make our country better. I am very happy that someone like Teddy Riner, who is a great champion, has decided to take part in this presidential debate and bring his convictions, his ideas and his talent,“ Macron continued.

schema.headline: French Judo Legend Teddy Riner Announces 2027 Presidential Bid, Drawing Praise From Emmanuel Macron

title: ‘Ramayana’ Makes History as First Indian Film to Top U.K., Ireland Box Office as ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Debuts in Third
description: Sony’s animated mythological adventure “Ramayana: Rise of a Legend” made history by becoming the first Indian feature ever to debut atop the U.K. a
body:
Sony’s animated mythological adventure “Ramayana: Rise of a Legend” made history by becoming the first Indian feature ever to debut atop the U.K. and Ireland box office, collecting £2.1 million ($2.8 million) to lead a crowded slate of new releases and push Anime Ltd.’s “Godzilla Minus Zero” into third place.

	The previous box office ceiling for Indian cinema in the territory was second place, held jointly by S.S. Rajamouli’s “RRR” in 2022, Shah Rukh Khan starrers “Pathaan” and “Jawan” in 2023 and Ranveer Singh’s “Dhurandhar: The Revenge” earlier this year.
	

	Disney’s “Wild Horse Nine” secured second position in its opening frame, taking $1.9 million. Anime Ltd.’s “Godzilla Minus Zero” claimed third place, generating $1.8 million.

	Black Bear’s period comedy “Wicker,” which led the chart in the previous session, moved to fourth place in its sophomore frame, collecting $1.5 million to push its running total to $5.7 million. Universal’s concert presentation “George Michael: The Faith Tour” debuted in fifth position, generating $1.3 million.

	A24’s “Primetime,” directed by Lance Oppenheim and starring Robert Pattinson, followed in sixth position in its second weekend, adding $1.1 million to elevate its total to $4.6 million. Lionsgate U.K.’s comedy horror “Ghosts: The Possession of Button House” took seventh spot in its third frame, collecting $997,064 to raise its cumulative gross to $10.3 million.

	Warner Bros.’ DC horror thriller “Clayface” landed in eighth place in its third session, generating $911,261 to take its running cume to $8.1 million. Entertainment Film Distributors’ biographical drama “I Play Rocky,” starring Anthony Ippolito, opened in ninth place with $810,781. Trafalgar Releasing’s event presentation of “Stray Kids World Tour ‘Run It’ Live Viewing” rounded out the top 10 in its debut weekend with $793,559.
	

	Just outside the top 10, Altitude’s Cannes winner “La Bola Negra” debuted in No. with 721,301. Meanwhile, Mubi’s “Fatherland,” directed by Paweł Pawlikowski and starring Sandra Hüller, maintained its foothold in its third weekend, ranking at No. 24 with $74,401 to lift its cumulative total to $997,741.

	Looking ahead to the upcoming theatrical frame, mid-week programming begins on Tuesday with Trafalgar Releasing presenting the live cinema broadcast of the Royal Ballet and Opera’s production of “Carmen – RBO, London 2026”, followed on Thursday by Dreamz Entertainment releasing Indian title “Vidudala”.

	Wide commercial and saturation rollouts arriving on Friday across 300+ locations are led by Susanna White’s legal drama “Prima Facie,” starring Cynthia Erivo, Daniel Ings, Toheeb Jimoh, and Noma Dumezweni. Studio platform and mid-tier rollouts include Sony’s “How To Rob A Bank”; Paramount’s holiday drama “Ebenezer”; Apple Original Films’ biographical drama “Being Heumann”; Picturehouse Entertainment’s Cannes winner “Fjord”; and Dartmouth Films’ nature documentary “Whispers In The Woods.”

	Specialized, festival, and international rollouts debuting Friday include Netflix’s wartime football drama “The Mosquito Bowl,” directed by Peter Berg and starring Nicholas Galitzine and Bill Skarsgård; Dreamz Entertainment’s dual Indian releases “Mega158” and “Kaaka”; Day For Night’s “100 Sunset,” directed by Kunsang Kyirong; Guerilla Films’ documentary “1 In 2,” directed by David Nicholas Wilkinson; Miracle/ESPN’s sports feature “Give Me The Ball!”; and DocHouse’s “A Fox Under a Pink Moon.”

	Repertory screenings are anchored by Park Circus launching the 20th anniversary 4K restoration of Sofia Coppola’s “Marie Antoinette,” starring Kirsten Dunst, Jason Schwartzman, and Steve Coogan, alongside Studiocanal’s 50th anniversary 4K restoration of Nicolas Roeg’s “The Man Who Fell To Earth,” starring David Bowie.

	The weekend wraps on Saturday with Dreamz Entertainment’s Indian release “George Krish”; Trafalgar Releasing’s event screening “Festive Fun With Peppa”; and Piece Of Magic Entertainment presenting the live cinema broadcast of the “League Of Legends Worlds 26 – Finals In Cinema”.

schema.headline: ‘Ramayana’ Makes History as First Indian Film to Top U.K., Ireland Box Office as ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Debuts in Third

title: ‘De Gaulle,’ ‘La Gradiva’ and ‘Alice: Pioneer Of Cinema’ Among American French Film Fest Winners- Film News in Brief
description:
The American French Film Festival announced the winners of this year’s awards during the closing ceremony on Nov. 8.

	The films were voted on by a
body:
The American French Film Festival announced the winners of this year’s awards during the closing ceremony on Nov. 8.

	The films were voted on by audiences attending the festival, members of the Los Angeles Film Critics Association, a jury of entertainment professionals and a student jury consisting of high school and college-age participants from the TAFFF High School Screenings Program.


	“De Gaulle,” written by Antonin Baudry and Bérénice Vila, directed by Antonin Baudry and Niels Schneider, Benoît Magimel and Anamaria Vartolomei, took home the Audience Award and top honor for best film.
	

	The Critics Award for best film was given to “La Gradiva.” Written by Marine Atlan and Anne Brouillet, the film is directed by Marine Atlan and stars Colas Quignard, Antonia Buresi, Mitia Capellier-Audat and Suzanne Gerin.

	“A Place For Her” received the First Feature Award; “Whispers In The Woods” received the Documentary Film Award; “The Green Eyes” received American Students Award; “Alice: Pioneer Of Cinema” received the Audience Series Award; “Swapped” received the Jury Series Award; “Diego” received the Audience Short Film Award; “God is Shy” received the Jury Short Film Award.
	
		Monday Nov. 9	

	Diversity and Inclusion Film Festival Set for N.Y.’s Lincoln Center

	The Distribution Collective will host the annual Diversity and Inclusion Film Festival at the Lincoln Center campus from Nov. 13 to Nov. 15.

	Special programming will include a Universal Studio Group panel on Nov. 14, featuring Hanako Greensmith (“Chicago Fire”), Zeeko Zaki (“FBI”) and David Ajala (“Law & Order”), who will discuss carrying forward the legacy of Wolf Entertainment’s iconic television franchises while introducing new dimensions to beloved series. 
	

	“DIFF was founded on the belief that storytelling has the power to bring communities together, challenge perceptions and create lasting opportunities for artists whose voices deserve to be heard,” said Sola Fasehun, the festival’s founder. “Our continued film festival at Lincoln Center in New York reflects that commitment in action. For several years, we’ve had the opportunity to introduce New York audiences to an incredible range of filmmakers through our programming, and we’re thrilled to be back at Lincoln Center for another year of welcoming filmmakers and supporting film and TV.”

schema.headline: ‘De Gaulle,’ ‘La Gradiva’ and ‘Alice: Pioneer Of Cinema’ Among American French Film Fest Winners- Film News in Brief

title: Julia Garner Says Madonna Biopic Status Changes ‘Every Hour,’ But She’d ‘Love for the Movie to Get Made’
description:
Julia Garner has given an ambiguous update on the long-delayed Madonna biopic, which has made little progress since its 2020 announcement.

	During
body:
Julia Garner has given an ambiguous update on the long-delayed Madonna biopic, which has made little progress since its 2020 announcement.

	During a recent interview with CBS, the actress was asked about the film’s status, to which she responded: “I don’t know. Every hour it changes, in a way.” “It’s not up to me. I would love for the movie to get made, obviously. But I also feel whatever happens, I made a great friend,” she continued. “I love Madonna. I think she’s incredible.”
	

	The last update Garner gave on the biopic was in July 2025, when she guested on the “SmartLess” podcast and told hosts Will Arnett, Sean Hayes and Jason Bateman that she was still set to star as the seven-time Grammy winner in the film. “That’s supposed to still happen,” Garner said, adding that she’s “such a fan of Madonna” and that she “grew up listening” to her music. She also assured fans that “anything that’s great…takes a long time,” referring to the delayed film.

	Back in 2023, Variety reported that the film had been scrapped ahead of Madonna’s world tour and would remain on pause indefinitely at Universal Pictures. Variety also exclusively reported that Garner landed the part in 2022 after a grueling process that included a full-on singing-and-dancing boot camp. Florence Pugh, Alexa Demie, Odessa Young and Bebe Rexha were also reported to have been in consideration for the role.

	The pop icon herself was set to direct, while two different scripts were reportedly penned by Diablo Cody (their writing sessions were widely disseminated on social media) and Cressida Wilson.
	

	Garner stars in Netflix’s “The Altrusists,” which tells the story of Sam Bankman-Fried (Anthony Boyle) and Caroline Ellison (Garner), “two hyper-smart, ambitious young idealists who tried to remake the global financial system in the blink of an eye — before they were accused of stealing $8 billion.” The eight-episode limited series hits the streamer on Nov. 19.

schema.headline: Julia Garner Says Madonna Biopic Status Changes ‘Every Hour,’ But She’d ‘Love for the Movie to Get Made’

title: Jon Stewart Breaks Down Trump’s ‘60 Minutes’ Interview: ‘Young Man, Was That Sass?’
description: On Monday night’s episode of “The Daily Show,” Jon Stewart celebrated being back behind the desk for the first time since the Blue Wave swept acros
body:
On Monday night’s episode of “The Daily Show,” Jon Stewart celebrated being back behind the desk for the first time since the Blue Wave swept across the U.S. during last week’s midterm elections, then promptly shifted his focus to Trump’s peculiar “60 Minutes” interview that aired Sunday.

	“Donald Trump headed over to the newly MAGA-fied CBS for a little self-soothing with one of ‘60 Minutes’’ new correspondents, a religious conservative by the name of Ross Douthat,” said Stewart before showing clips that saw the interviewer push back on Trump throughout. Talking about the increase in Trump’s net worth since returning to the White House, Douthat pressed: “My net worth did not go up by $3 billion.”
	

	“Young man, was that sass? Did the newly MAGA-fied CBS ’60 Minutes’ just deliver sass to Donald Trump? I think you’re supposed to ‘Yes, and,’ not ‘Yes, but,” laughed Stewart. “I think I’m going to enjoy this. I did not come into this interview thinking I’m going to enjoy this.” The host continued to point out that earlier in the interview, Trump had said his “best thing” was money and finance, but minutes later, feigned ignorance over his worth, saying, “I guess it’s gone up. I don’t even know.” “So when it’s global finance, Trump is Keanu Reeves from ‘The Matrix,’ but when it’s his own $3 billion post-election windfall, he’s Keanu Reeves from ‘Bill and Ted,’” joked Stewart.

	Stewart then poked fun at several questions Douthat asked, including “What do you think happens when you die?” “You want Trump to answer one of the great philosophical questions of our existence? He doesn’t even know where money comes from,” said Stewart. The host commended the “artistic choice” made by “60 Minutes” to “cut away from the interview and go to commercial for maximum dramatic impact” after Trump said he could not forgive his enemies (like James Comey and Nancy Pelosi), even if it was the only way he could get into heaven.
	

	Stewart also took aim at Trump’s new Chief of Staff Stephen Miller with the help of comedian Jordan Klepper. Following his monologue, Stewart was joined by Rachel Maddow on Monday’s episode, which he joked is a “liberal’s wet dream.”

	Check out the entire monologue below.

schema.headline: Jon Stewart Breaks Down Trump’s ‘60 Minutes’ Interview: ‘Young Man, Was That Sass?’

title: ‘Ebenezer’ First Reactions: Johnny Depp’s Hollywood Comeback Is a ‘Wickedly Fun Holiday Treat’ That Adds ‘Refreshing New Layers’ to the Christmas Classic
description: “Ebenezer” has officially premiered, and reviews for the Johnny Depp-led film are largely positive among members of the film press, who are praisin
body:
“Ebenezer” has officially premiered, and reviews for the Johnny Depp-led film are largely positive among members of the film press, who are praising the star’s return to Hollywood as a “wickedly fun holiday treat” that functions as a “strong comeback vehicle for its star.” 

	UK Film Critic Phil Roberts commended the film as a “bold spin on Dickens’ classic, delivering a sincere period piece infused with heart and despair.” “Johnny Depp is magnetic throughout Scrooge’s soft redemption arc leading to a finale that delivers more emotional resonance than its predecessors,” he wrote on X. “Humbug!” 
	

	Tom Chatalbash, FilmSpeak’s chief film critic, called “Ebenezar” a “wickedly fun holiday treat and strong comeback vehicle for its star,” he wrote, going on to praise Depp’s performance. “Depp is a fiendish delight as Scrooge, delivering a lively performance that thankfully balances the goofy charm and emotional gravitas that has been sorely missed. West’s horror sensibilities and visual panache give the film an immersive gothic look and feel as he’s able to balance the macabre thrills with the heart of Dickens’ beloved tale as he sprinkles in some refreshing new layers to deepen Ebenezer’s journey. Simply put, it’s great to see Depp back on the big screen. Full review soon!” 

	“#Ebenezer is a pleasant surprise,” wrote Critics Choice member Clarence Moye. “Ti West brings a lovely gothic visual style which helps freshen an otherwise standard take. And of course Depp is great, standing with George C. Scott as the best of the modern Scrooges.” Fellow Critics Choice member Tony Mosello similarly enjoyed the film, calling it a “revitalized edition of the classic Victorian fable of redemption, centered around a fun, quirky, and energetic Johnny Depp performance. Ti West captures the gothic horror vibes to combine them with some intriguing and haunting visuals and solid supporting cast.” 
	

	However, not every review was complimentary. “I’m a sucker for A Christmas Carol & #Ebenezer hits all the beats right, but nothing’s distinct or unique about this version,” wrote film critic Ren Vieira, who was less approving. “Fantastic set design, production & sound design, but it’s just Depp doing cooky Scrooge, nothing more than his old tricks… Claflin & Grint innocent.”

	UK-based film critic and writer MaryAnn Johanson kept her similarly unfavorable assessment short and sweet: “Utterly superfluous,” she wrote on X. 

	“EBENEZER is fine I guess,” wrote film critic Robert Ortiz. “Technically well made and Johnny Depp certainly looks and acts the part but the film commits 2 sins of being forgettable and just boring, especially if you’ve seen a Christmas carol before. Doesn’t do anything new and fails to justify its existence.”

	“Ebenezer” reimagines the Christmas classic “A Christmas Carol,” this time starring Depp as Scrooge. Directed by Ti West, the description simply reads: “The name you know, the story you don’t.” Alongside Depp, “Ebenezer” boasts an ensemble including Rupert Grint, Andrea Riseborough, Sam Claflin, Daisy Ridley, Arthur Conti, Ellie Bamber, Henry Lloyd-Hughes, Charlie Murphy, Tramell Tillman and Ian McKellen.

	Notably, the film is the first Hollywood studio film Depp has done since his highly publicized 2022 trial against ex-wife Amber Heard, during which both accused the other of domestic abuse and defamation. (Depp was ultimately awarded $10 million in compensatory damages and $5 million in punitive damages from Heard, while Heard was awarded $2 million in compensatory damages.) Thus, “Ebenezer” is functioning as — or at least was aimed to be — a major comeback for the “Edward Scissorhands” actor.

	“Ebenezer” is set to hit theaters on Nov. 13 from Paramount. Check out first reactions in the posts below.

title: How the American French Film Festival Is Bringing French Cinema to 3,000 Los Angeles High School Students With Packed Screenings of ‘In Waves’
description: The American French Film Festival, which celebrated its 30th anniversary this year, has been on a journey to cultivate a new generation of French m
body:
The American French Film Festival, which celebrated its 30th anniversary this year, has been on a journey to cultivate a new generation of French movie lovers for two decades with its educational program for Los Angeles high school students. 

	This milestone edition brought around 3,000 students to the DGA theater for five packed screenings of “In Waves,” Phuong Mai Nguyen’s heart-wrenching animated feature which was bought Netflix at Cannes. 
	

	Adapted from AJ Dungo’s graphic novel at set in Southern California, “In Waves” is a love story between a shy teenage boy and the girl who teaches him how to surf and how to live, before she succumbs to cancer. 

	The screenings, which drew applause and tears throughout, also gave students the opportunity to engage in the post-screening Q&A with the film’s producer, Priscilla Bertin, and screenwriter Fanny Burdino. 



	

									Philip Guerette
	



	Spearheaded by Anouchka Van Riel, the festival deputy director, the program brings together more than 60 schools over five days, with roughly half coming from the public school system and half from private institutions. It also reaches beyond French-language classes to students studying performing arts and other creative disciplines.

	In an interview with Variety, Van Riel discussed the importance of the programme to allow younger audiences to discover international cinema at a time when arthouse moviegoers are aging and foreign-language films face growing challenges in U.S. theaters. She also talked about the program’s rapid growth, why subtitles are no longer the barrier they once were, and the powerful response to “In Waves” which Netflix is positioning in the Awards race. 
	

	How many students and schools participate in the program?

	We have more than 60 schools participating over five days, so that’s more than 12 schools a day. We organize five screenings of the same film, each with around 600 students. That’s approximately 3,000 students every year. I’ve built a database of around 300 schools, and we start reaching out in May. Within a week of sending the first email, half the seats — around 1,500 — are already booked. Then I spend the summer filling the remaining places. There’s enormous demand. We also make a point of having a mix of public and private schools, roughly 50/50. That’s very important to us. For public schools, transportation can be a challenge. Some have to apply for grants just to pay for the buses. There’s an entire economy around organizing these trips, and a lot depends on the teachers.



	

									Philip Guerette
	



	How does the festival work with teachers to prepare students for the screenings?

	We work with the American Association of Teachers of French, which prepares two educational guides, one in French and one in English. The French-language guide is around 100 pages long. It’s incredibly detailed and allows teachers to explore the film from multiple perspectives, including its themes and cinematic language. The guides are designed to help students study the film before or after the screening. And we don’t just work with French-language classes. Around half of the participating classes are English-speaking. Many Los Angeles high schools have performing arts programs, and those students come because they’re interested in cinema and want to meet the filmmakers. The majority of these kids have never attended a film screening followed by a Q&A. That’s something we want to change.

	That’s surprising in Los Angeles, where the film industry is everywhere.

	It’s extraordinary. I’m a member of the Producers Guild, and I receive invitations to screenings and conversations with filmmakers almost every day. There are incredible events happening constantly, but these kids don’t have access to them. Of course, if their parents work in the industry, that’s different. But otherwise, most students aren’t exposed to that world. I grew up in a small town in Alsace, and I remember my French teacher taking us to the movies all the time when I was in middle school. Some of those screenings even had Q&As. There’s a tradition of that in France that doesn’t really exist here in the same way. We used to organize masterclasses for university students, including at USC, but we realized it was difficult to attract them. They’re already surrounded by so many opportunities on campus. With high school students, we can work directly through the teachers. That’s how we’ve developed this program.
	

	Is the goal ultimately to cultivate a younger audience for French cinema?

	Absolutely. It’s about renewing the audience. A couple of years ago, we screened “The Marching Band,” and when the film was eventually released theatrically in the U.S., I was invited to moderate a Q&A. I loved the film, so I was very happy to do it. But the theater was only half full, and I don’t think there was a single person under 65. That’s the problem. Foreign-language films have traditionally been considered niche in the U.S. Streaming platforms have helped change that perception somewhat, but we still need to familiarize younger audiences with these films. That’s why this program is so important.

	Are subtitles still an obstacle for younger American audiences?

	Not nearly as much as people think. We’ve conducted surveys with students after the screenings, and more than 80% say subtitles aren’t a barrier to watching foreign-language films. It’s not a completely scientific study, but it gives us a good indication of how attitudes are changing. Between streaming platforms, social media and series like “Squid Game,” young people have become accustomed to watching subtitled content. Sometimes there’s still a little hesitation before the screening. But once they’re sitting in the theater, they realize it’s easy. I really don’t think subtitles are the problem for this generation anymore. Distribution is a major part of the problem. That’s why streaming platforms have become so important for the circulation of foreign-language films. But there’s also the question of exposure. If young people aren’t given opportunities to discover these films, they’re not necessarily going to seek them out themselves.



	

					In Waves
									Courtesy of Netflix
	



	This year’s selection was “In Waves.” What made it particularly suitable for the program?

	There’s a wonderful connection between this film and the festival. The producer, Priscilla Bertin, had already come to the festival two years ago with “Wild Diamond,” and at the time she was in post-production on “In Waves.” We became familiar with the project very early, and it made complete sense for us to bring it back this year. What’s interesting is that the film is based on an American graphic novel that was discovered by a French producer in a secondhand bookstore in France and developed into a movie. We explain that background to the students before the screenings, including why it’s considered a French film and the response has been extraordinary.
	

	The screenings were packed, and the students seemed particularly moved by the film. What was the atmosphere like?

	It was very striking. At the first screening, I went straight into introducing the filmmakers for the Q&A, and I realized something wasn’t right because the students were still processing what they’d just watched. Usually, when a film ends, the students immediately line up to ask questions. But with “In Waves,” it took time. Every day, there was this moment of silence. The film had affected them so deeply that they needed a little time before they could speak. There’s something cathartic about sitting in a dark theater with other people, crying together and sharing the same emotions. You feel safe because everyone is experiencing that grief together. I think young people have fewer opportunities to experience cinema that way now. That’s what made these screenings so special.

schema.headline: How the American French Film Festival Is Bringing French Cinema to 3,000 Los Angeles High School Students With Packed Screenings of ‘In Waves’

title: Saylor Hayes' Cause of Death Revealed Months After 5-Year-Old Found Dead
description:
Saylor Hayes
                          Cause of Death Revealed
body:
Saylor Hayes
                          Cause of Death Revealed
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 9, 2026
                            6:10 PM PST
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The mystery surrounding 5-year-old Saylor Hayes' death is becoming a little clearer ... officials announced Monday she died from drowning, months after her body was discovered in a South Carolina river.
      
    
            The Georgetown County Coroner's Office determined Saylor died from asphyxia due to drowning, with child neglect listed as a contributing factor.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            However, officials say they still can't determine whether her death was an accident or homicide.
      

            The coroner's office explained ... "This classification reflects the inability to conclusively determine whether Saylor’s death was accidental or the result of a homicidal act."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            As we previously reported, Saylor's autopsy was conducted in September. The examination revealed pulmonary edema -- a buildup of fluid in the lungs -- but found no signs of external or internal trauma.
      
    
            Saylor's parents, John Herb Hayes III and Geordyn Nichole Hayes, were arrested in connection with her death and charged with unlawfully placing a child at risk/willfully abandoning a child.

title: Nvidia: Securities Class Action Lawsuit Filed Amid CEO's Affair with Alleged Chinese Spy
description:
Nvidia
                          Facing Lawsuit Claiming Company Made False Statements
body:
Nvidia
                          Facing Lawsuit Claiming Company Made False Statements
                          Related to CEO's Affair
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              
                November 9, 2026
                
                            3:08 PM PST
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  November 9, 2026
                                4:14 PM PST
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s admitted affair with an alleged Chinese spy has now resulted in a securities class action lawsuit against his company ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            According to court documents, obtained by TMZ, the tech company allegedly violated federal securities laws by making misleading and false statements in connection with the scandal.
      
    
            The lawsuit calls into question several statements made by the company in response to multiple news articles about Jensen’s business relationship with Alice Huang -- the Megaspeed exec at the center of the affair story … who some claim is a Chinese spy.
      

            The suit alleges that Jensen and Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo both made statements about the nature of the business relationship with Megaspeed that were misleading or false, claiming Jensen had been having an affair with Alice at the time.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            According to the lawsuit, once news broke about the alleged affair, Nvidia stock plummeted, causing “significant losses and damages” to shareholders of the company.
      
    
            The plaintiffs identified in the class action include anyone who purchased or acquired publicly traded shares of Nvidia between October 9, 2025, and November 8, 2026.
      
    
            The class action is seeking monetary damages for losses sustained as a result of the allegedly false and misleading statements.

title: 'Deadliest Catch' Boat F/V Wizard Will Not Be Featured on Upcoming Season
description:
'Deadliest Catch'
                          F/V Wizard Will Not Appear in Upcoming Season
body:
'Deadliest Catch'
                          F/V Wizard Will Not Appear in Upcoming Season
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 9, 2026
                            5:50 PM PST
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            It's time for the F/V Wizard to cast off ... because the iconic vessel won't be featured in the upcoming season of "Deadliest Catch," TMZ has learned.
      
    
            Sources familiar with the situation tell TMZ ... the vessel wasn't kicked off the show ... but production is not currently filming aboard the F/V Wizard for the fall season.
      
    
            We're told this isn't out of character for the Discovery Channel series -- "Deadliest Catch" routinely rotates vessels for all sorts of reasons.
      

            The F/V Wizard has been a mainstay since Season 3, and has been continuously for 20 seasons ... meaning this will be the first time the vessel won't be featured since it joined the show.
      
    
            Season 23 is currently in production ... and no word yet on whether F/V Wizard will be brought back in the future.
      
    
            We reached out to captain Keith Colburn and he declined to comment.
